messages:
maria: Heads-up — on the Hera-PTQ canary I started seeing a spike in funcall JSON parse failures after enabling continuous batching. Parse failures were ~0.6% baseline, jumped to ~4.9% within an hour.

maria: Example response (raw):
```json
{"tool":"lookup","args":{"id":123},"result":{"name":"widget"}}>>>
```

raj: Which exact build? is this the v1.3-ptq that landed yesterday? also: what batching config (max_batch_size / latency target)?

maria: It’s hera-ptq v1.3. Batch config is continuous batching on, max_batch_size=64, latency target=80ms. Canary at 5% traffic.

kevin: My guess: partial-token termination + kvcache/prefix interleaving. Quant models sometimes emit extra trailing tokens when batched/streamed. Try disabling continuous batching or set max_batch_size=1 as a quick probe.

kevin: Also try turning off streaming (we stream token-by-token which can create partial JSON at reconnect).

sasha: Quick experiment plan:
- run micro-canary with continuous batching off, batch_size=1
- run with kvcache.prefix_fallback=true
- add a temporary postprocess that wraps output in a tolerant JSON wrapper (strip trailing non-JSON) and measure 

deploy-bot: canary deploy: hera-ptq v1.3-ptq -> 5% @ 2024-11-02T09:02:41Z. autoscale: ok.

maria: I kicked off three probes: 1) batch=64 streaming on, 2) batch=1 streaming on, 3) batch=64 streaming off. Results (1000 samples each):
- probe1 parse_fail_rate=4.9%
- probe2 parse_fail_rate=0.7%
- probe3 parse_fail_rate=1.1%
Link to eval: https://console.redwood/evals/hera-ptq/1745554321

kevin: Nice. That points squarely at batching/streaming interaction. If batch=1 looks fine, we can try enabling batching with a kvcache flush point at request boundaries or add an end-sentinel to the funcall contract. e.g. require `\n--END_TOOL_CALL--` suffix from model.

raj: Also request logits + tokenizer boundary around the truncated token for a few failures — need to rule out tokenizer/kernel emitting control characters. If we see controlchar (0x1e/0x03) near EOF that's a kernel artifact.

sasha: I can run an int8 vs int4 micro-canary in dedicated (no shared kvcache) to compare. If dedicated+batching still fails, that suggests model/kernel rather than routing.

eval-bot: sampled_failures: 49/1000 (probe1), 7/1000 (probe2), 11/1000 (probe3). Added failure examples: samples/1745554321/failures.tar.gz

maria: I pulled a few raw tokens around EOF — saw repeated \u001f characters in three failures. Attaching one snippet: ``..."result":{...}}\u001f\u001f>>>``

kevin: ok that smells like a control-char leak. Two mitigations: 1) model compilation flag suppress_partial_eos=true (skip emitting special control sequences at stream boundaries) 2) route canary through dedicated nodes with isolated kvcache to isolate KV-prefix races.

sasha: I'll queue a build with suppress_partial_eos and run a 1k sample micro-canary with batching=32 and streaming on. If that fixes it we can roll to 20% before wide rollout.

maria: Thanks — also adding a short-term client-side rescue: tolerant_json_strip(response_text) that trims trailing non-json up to last `}` and tries parse, and expose a retry that forces batch=1 for that request. Implementing now.

raj: +1 on the rescue. Also add a telemetry tag for "truncated_ctrlchar" so we can slice by model/build/region.

kevin: tl;dr: likely interaction of continuous batching + streaming + control-char emission from quantized model. Plan: (1) rescue parser + retry budget bump, (2) micro-canary of suppress_partial_eos build, (3) compare dedicated vs shared kvcache, (4) add end-sentinel contract if we keep streaming.

maria: Will run the suppress_partial_eos micro-canary and post numbers here in ~30m. Thanks all :thumbsup: :robot_face:
__notes: no title field per agents.md; messages is a single continuous Slack thread string
